decisions.reason: As a more specialized particle-therapy water phantom with some market access still unfolding, it is costlier and more uncertain than the chamber products, but the uncertainty itself preserves option value so management would likely keep it for now.
This small-volume ionization chamber sits squarely in the firm's core dosimetry capability, likely has low carrying cost, and has not yet shown evidence that its value will not materialize.
As another closely related small-volume ionization chamber, it appears to be an incremental extension of the established portfolio whose option value still exceeds its likely maintenance cost.
A standard clinical ionization chamber line with several models fits mainstream clinical demand and suggests a broader commercial commitment, making withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.
The relative-dosimetry chamber is a focused but complementary product in the firm's core market, and absent clear negative signals management would usually preserve the option.
The thimble ionization chamber is a conventional adjacent offering that likely shares technology and support resources with the existing business, so keeping it is more attractive than an early exit.
